text:
ravi: FYI — onboarding report: sampleapp auth flakes when rotating creds in env; new hires can't reproduce with CLI; they're stuck.
emily: Can you paste the error?
ravi: `401 Invalid key scope` from SDK call after env var rotate. Only happens if REDWOOD_API_KEY is swapped but REDWOOD_PROJECT not set.
jen: Ah — sampleapp README only mentions REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ORG, not REDWOOD_PROJECT. Docs mismatch.
kevin: Node SDK currently uses REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME instead of REDWOOD_PROJECT (legacy). Python uses REDWOOD_PROJECT. Oops.
sam: That explains it. New CI templates export REDWOOD_PROJECT but not PROJECT_NAME.
ravi: Repro steps from new hire: 1) set REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxxx 2) unset REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME 3) start sampleapp -> 401.
emily: We should make SDKs fallback: check REDWOOD_PROJECT, then REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME, then --project flag. Also log clear msg about missing project scoping.
jen: :thumbsup: + update sampleapp README and onboarding checklist (call out env var names and preferred precedence).
kevin: I'll open a quick PR to Node SDK for fallback and parity. Assigning to @kevin.
deploy-bot: CI: node-sdk-parity #123 — tests queued ✅
sam: Also rotation problem: ephemeral creds rotated by CI sometimes produce short-lived tokens; SDK retries are swallowing 401s as transient and retrying forever. Need explicit non-retry for auth failures.
ravi: Good catch. Treat 401/403 as non-retry unless header `Retry-After` is present. Also add a clear error message about scope mismatch (e.g., "API key missing project scope: set REDWOOD_PROJECT").
jen: Can we ship docs patch today and SDK fix in next patch release? New hires are blocked on onboarding.
kevin: I can do docs now, SDK fix PR in a couple hours. Will add a CHANGES entry and a small test.
emily: I’ll update the onboarding checklist and add a smoke test to sampleapp that validates project env var present at startup.
ravi: Thanks all. Follow-ups: kevin PR link, emily update checklist, ops to notify support. Filing a tiny incident for onboarding friction (low sev).
